overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation over the 'NEW/OLD BUSINESS' notice heading, declined to review the weekday-scheduling allegation, and reminded the Board of its complaint-response deadlines, advising but not ordering a change in the heading.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the posted notices' 'NEW/OLD BUSINESS' heading did not show which listed topics were new and which had previously come before the Board.
allegations.key_passage: However, we do not find that this heading rose to the level of an Open Meeting Law violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board scheduled a meeting on a weekday to reduce the number of people who might attend.
allegations.key_passage: Even if proven true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaints; the AG noted the Board did not respond to either complaint until contacted by the AG's office.
allegations.key_passage: Unless an extension of time has been requested, a public body must, within 14 business days of receipt of an Open Meeting Law complaint, meet to review the complaint, send a copy of the complaint to the Attorney General's Office, and notify the Attorney General of any remedial action taken.
